thread:
maya: Heads-up — east1 preemptible eviction spike, ~18% over the last hour. Mostly hitting mixed-capacity pools running gpt-small-v2 variants. Some customer errors (timeouts) reported.

devon: Ugh. Any upstream network flakiness or is this capacity churn?

maya: Looks like spot churn + a couple of AZs reporting API throttles from the provider. No network packet loss on our side.

liam: Can we fanout to warm reserved capacity in us-east-2 and fallback to cpu-q8 variants for non-enterprise traffic? Trade latency for stability.

maya: Yep — that matches my thinking. Priority: keep enterprise SLAs on reserved GPUs, spill non-critical traffic to cheaper variants/regions.

sre-bot: [alert] provider-east1: spot-evictions=18%, throttled-instances=12, avg-queue-ms=2400

devon: Plan sketch: 1) soft-failover to us-east-2/central as primary region for new requests, 2) variant fallback chain: canonical -> quantized-gpu -> quantized-cpu, 3) per-tenant policy: enterprise bypass fallback. Thoughts?

alex: +1. Need to cap fanout concurrency when failing across regions to avoid cascading costs. Suggest token-bucket limiter and failure budget per-route.

liam: Also add a quick probe before routing: single-token fast-latency probe to candidate pools to avoid sending bulk traffic into a saturated lane. Probe interval 10s, timeout 500ms.

maya: Putting a minimal route policy here (pseudo-yaml):

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  - condition: tenant.tier == "enterprise"
    action: prefer: reserved-east1
  - condition: evictions.region(east1) > 10%
    action:
      - route: us-east-2
        concurrency_limit: 200
        probe: {interval_ms: 10000, timeout_ms: 500}
      - variant_fallback_chain:
          - name: gpt-small-v2
            prefer: gpu-quant
          - name: gpt-small-v2-q8
            prefer: cpu-quant
cost_controls:
  non_enterprise_max_spill_cost_per_min: 2.50
  fanout_token_bucket: {rate: 50, burst: 200}
```

devon: Can we wire this into the router with a canary? E.g., 5% of non-enterprise requests for 15m, then 25% if stable.

maya: Yes — add rollout config: canary 5% x 15m -> ramp 25% x 30m -> full. Also auto-revert on error-rate > 1.5x baseline.

liam: For short-lived bursts we should avoid spinning up new reserved nodes. Use warm standby pools with preloaded KV caches to reduce cold-start penalty. Keep warm pool size dynamic by short-term PID: target = max(10, inflight_qps/50).

alex: One more: telemetry tags on fallback paths so cost/latency gets attributed correctly (route=region-failover, variant=cpu-q8, fallback_reason=preemptive-eviction). Will help econometrics.

maya: Ops checklist for now:
- enable soft-failover policy in router (canary 5%)
- enable token-bucket limits and probe
- reserve 100 GPU slots in us-east-2 for enterprise SLA
- spin warm standby pool (size 20) for mixed-capacity nodes

devon: I'll create the PR for router config + rollout plan.

liam: I'll handle standby pool scaling hook and probe implementation.

alex: I'll add telemetry and cost tags to the tracing pipeline.

maya: Thanks. If eviction rate passes 25% we escalate to mandatory region evacuation and notify eng-sre. :rotating_light:

sre-bot: [action] created incident #INF-4726: east1-spot-eviction-uptick

maya: Good call. Keep updates minimal in this thread; post major status to #incidents and tag eng-sre.

devon: Roger. PR incoming in ~30m. :thumbsup:
